claims.claim_vi: The source covers leap seconds (23:59:60), the bugs they cause in time-processing code, and which time representations need to handle them.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Leap seconds exist because the Earth's rotation is not uniform against atomic time; software assuming 60-second minutes can fail; Unix timestamps treat each day as 86,400 s; smearing spreads the extra second over a long window; abolishing leap seconds removes the extra second but lets civil time drift from the Sun.
claims.verified_by: General knowledge of the author, not checked against an official document: the writing environment could only reach GitHub, and no official document for this topic is hosted there.
